text.p: *For the second SYCOM session in a row the Australian 10-year bond futures contract was repelled from the low-93.300s as it attempted to bounce back after the recent negative tone.
*U.S. Treasuries were firm, but below the day's highs, after the July PPI fell 0.1 percent and retail sales grew 0.6 percent.
For the second SYCOM session in a row the September Australian 10-year bond futures contract was repelled from the low-93.300s as it attempted bounce back after the recent negative tone.
The contract ended modestly higher at 93.230 compared with Wednesday's 93.200 close, but below a session high of 93.315.

"The capping of SYCOM ranges again by resistance near 93.310...suggests a few more days of consolidation under 93.310 is necessary before that resistance is cut and a recovery to 93.470 is seen," said Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac.
Pontikis expects the market will test support at 93.180/93.200, but the contract is likely to be confined to a 93.200/93.270 range on the day.

The long end has been under intense downward pressure for almost week, largely as a result of a weakening U.S. Treasury market, and since the beginning of the month the 10-year contract has slipped from an all time high of 93.695 to a low of 93.135 on Wednesday.
U.S. Treasuries firmed on Wednesday, but also finished below the day's highs after failing to follow-through a rally in response to July PPI and retail sales data.
Producer prices fell 0.1 percent and the seventh consecutive decline, and although retail sales were fairly solid at a 0.6 percent rise it was below the 1.0 percent-plus the market had been fearing.
The July U.S. CPI is due later on Thursday.
Locally, final average weekly wages data for the second quarter are due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
